zh.principle: **标准**：安全散列标准（Secure Hash Standard）。题页的宣告行写「Announcing the SECURE HASH STANDARD」，文告第 1 条把名称与编号钉在一起：「1.Name of Standard: Secure Hash Standard (SHS) (FIPS PUB 180-4).」摘要给出自我定义：「This standard specifies hash algorithms that can be used to generate digests of messages.」下一句交代用途：「The digests are used to detect whether messages have been changed since the digests were generated.」第 3 条逐个点名算法并给出对象：「3.Explanation: This Standard specifies secure hash algorithms - SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 - for computing a condensed representation of electronic data (message).」同一节限定输出：「The message digests range in length from 160 to 512 bits, depending on the algorithm.」规定的是七个算法与摘要的计算方式，算法之外的强度判断另有文件。
zh.why: 理由写在第 3 条的第二段，用两条困难性定义 secure：「The hash algorithms specified in this Standard are called secure because, for a given algorithm, it is computationally infeasible 1) to find a message that corresponds to a given message digest, or 2) to find two different messages that produce the same message digest.」后果紧接一句：「This will result in a verification failure when the secure hash algorithm is used with a digital signature algorithm or a keyed-hash message authentication algorithm.」第 1 节给出结构前提：「All of the algorithms are iterative, one-way hash functions that can process a message to produce a condensed representation called a message digest.」三段连读是同一个论证：摘要能充当完整性判据，前提正是求原像与找碰撞都不可行，而这两条困难性就是本文所称 secure 的含义。
zh.used: 应用义务写在文告的适用与实现两条。第 6 条用 must 落到联邦用法：「Either this Standard or Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 202 must be implemented wherever a secure hash algorithm is required for Federal applications, including as a component within other cryptographic algorithms and protocols.」第 8 条先开放实现载体：「8.Implementations: The secure hash algorithms specified herein may be implemented in software, firmware, hardware or any combination thereof.」再给出合规关口：「Only algorithm implementations that are validated by NIST will be considered as complying with this standard.」两句层级不同：前者是联邦应用中 must 级的实现要求，后者把合规认定系于 NIST 验证，算法本身正确并不足以构成符合。
zh.broken: 三处限度均出自文件自身。第 12 条先否认符合即安全：「While it is the intent of this Standard to specify general security requirements for generating a message digest, conformance to this Standard does not assure that a particular implementation is secure.」并把判断交给使用方：「The responsible authority in each agency or department shall assure that an overall implementation provides an acceptable level of security.」强度问题则明确另交他文：「The algorithms differ most significantly in the security strengths that are provided for the data being hashed.」其下一句给出去处：「The security strengths of these hash functions and the system as a whole when each of them is used with other cryptographic algorithms, such as digital signature algorithms and keyed-hash message authentication codes, can be found in [SP 800-57] and [SP 800-107].」第 13 条又关掉豁免通道：「The Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) does not allow for waivers to a FIPS that is made mandatory by the Secretary of Commerce.」三处限制各有层级：符合本标准只担保摘要的产生方式，不担保被部署的实现整体可接受；强度的取值另见两份文件；被部长定为强制的 FIPS 不允许豁免。
zh.history: 题页两行连读为「Federal Information Processing Standards Publication 180-4 August 2015」，即这份副本的日期行是 2015 年 8 月；其下的免费获取行写「This publication is available free of charge from:」，其后是 DOI 10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4。前言署名为「Charles H.Romine, Director Information Technology Laboratory」；文告第 4 条把批准权写成「4.Approving Authority: Secretary of Commerce.」取代关系见第 3 条末句：「This Standard supersedes FIPS 180-3 [FIPS 180-3].」本文件没有作者栏，署名是商务部长、NIST 所长（兼标准与技术副部长）与信息技术实验室主任；这份留存文本只给出 2015 年 8 月的日期行与被取代的 180-3，未见 180-4 自身初版日期的记载。

en.principle: **Standard**: Secure Hash Standard (安全散列标准). The masthead announces "Announcing the SECURE HASH STANDARD" and clause 1 fixes name and number together: "1. Name of Standard: Secure Hash Standard (SHS) (FIPS PUB 180-4)." The abstract gives the self-definition: "This standard specifies hash algorithms that can be used to generate digests of messages." followed by the use: "The digests are used to detect whether messages have been changed since the digests were generated." Clause 3 names the algorithms and their object: "3. Explanation: This Standard specifies secure hash algorithms - SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 - for computing a condensed representation of electronic data (message)." and bounds the output: "The message digests range in length from 160 to 512 bits, depending on the algorithm." What is specified is the computation of the digests by these seven algorithms; judging strength is left to other documents.
en.why: The reason is stated in clause 3, where the two infeasibilities define the term: "The hash algorithms specified in this Standard are called secure because, for a given algorithm, it is computationally infeasible 1) to find a message that corresponds to a given message digest, or 2) to find two different messages that produce the same message digest." The consequence follows at once: "This will result in a verification failure when the secure hash algorithm is used with a digital signature algorithm or a keyed-hash message authentication algorithm." Clause 1 supplies the structural premise: "All of the algorithms are iterative, one-way hash functions that can process a message to produce a condensed representation called a message digest." Read together, a digest works as an integrity test only because finding the preimage and finding a collision are both infeasible, which is exactly what this document means by secure.
en.used: The application duties are in the applicability and implementation clauses. Clause 6 uses must for federal use: "Either this Standard or Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 202 must be implemented wherever a secure hash algorithm is required for Federal applications, including as a component within other cryptographic algorithms and protocols." Clause 8 first leaves the carrier open: "8. Implementations: The secure hash algorithms specified herein may be implemented in software, firmware, hardware or any combination thereof." then sets the gate: "Only algorithm implementations that are validated by NIST will be considered as complying with this standard." The two work at different levels: one is a must-level requirement to implement either this Standard or FIPS 202 wherever federal use demands a secure hash, the other makes compliance itself conditional on validation by NIST.
en.broken: Three limits are the document speaking about itself. Clause 12 denies that conformance is security: "While it is the intent of this Standard to specify general security requirements for generating a message digest, conformance to this Standard does not assure that a particular implementation is secure." and assigns the judgement: "The responsible authority in each agency or department shall assure that an overall implementation provides an acceptable level of security." Strength is handed to other documents: "The algorithms differ most significantly in the security strengths that are provided for the data being hashed." with the destination named: "The security strengths of these hash functions and the system as a whole when each of them is used with other cryptographic algorithms, such as digital signature algorithms and keyed-hash message authentication codes, can be found in [SP 800-57] and [SP 800-107]." Clause 13 closes the exemption route: "The Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) does not allow for waivers to a FIPS that is made mandatory by the Secretary of Commerce." The three operate at different levels: conformance covers how digests are produced, the strength figures live in two other publications, and a FIPS made mandatory admits no waiver.
en.history: The two masthead lines read in sequence "Federal Information Processing Standards Publication 180-4 August 2015", so this copy carries the date line August 2015; below it the free-access line reads "This publication is available free of charge from:" followed by the DOI 10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4. The foreword is signed "Charles H. Romine, Director Information Technology Laboratory"; clause 4 states the approving authority: "4. Approving Authority: Secretary of Commerce." and the supersession is the last sentence of clause 3: "This Standard supersedes FIPS 180-3 [FIPS 180-3]." The document has no author line; the names printed on it are the Secretary of Commerce, the NIST Director (Under Secretary for Standards and Technology) and the Director of the Information Technology Laboratory, and this retained copy records only the August 2015 date line and the superseded FIPS 180-3, not a first-publication date for 180-4 itself.

zh: message digest：散列算法对消息算出的输出，本文件中长 160 至 512 比特。
secure hash algorithm：本文件指定的七个算法的统称。
one-way hash function：由消息到摘要可算、由摘要反求消息不可行的函数。
preprocessing：哈希计算前的两步处理，含消息填充、分组解析与初始值设定。
truncated message digest：对较长摘要取左端若干比特得到的缩短结果。
en: Message digest: the output of a hash algorithm over a message, 160 to 512 bits in this Standard.
Secure hash algorithm: the collective name for the seven algorithms specified here.
SHA-2 family: SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256.
One-way hash function: computable from message to digest, infeasible to invert from digest to message.
Preprocessing: the steps before hash computation, covering padding, block parsing and the initial value.
Truncated message digest: the shortened result formed by taking leftmost bits of a longer digest.
